term: mind-independent, as moral objectivism (a metaphysical thesis)
definition: Moral objectivism: moral facts exist and are mind-independent in the relevant sense; with cognitivism and success theory it makes a view robust moral realism. Non-objectivism holds that moral facts exist and are mind-dependent. Both presuppose moral facts, so a noncognitivist is neither. Which mind-independence relation is meant is not fixed (Moral Anti-Realism §3.3 lists several and reports Tropman's attitude-independence account).
